exercises.instruction: What does the sentence mean? Pick the translation.

items.prompt: Ev sahibi mektubu almışsa cevap verir.
items.say: Ev sahibi mektubu almışsa cevap verir.
options: If the landlord got the letter, he'll reply
If the landlord had gotten the letter, he would have replied
The landlord got the letter and will reply
items.explanation: -mışsa — a live “if”: maybe he already got it. The door is open.

options: If I know in advance, I'll come
If I'd known in advance, I would have come
I knew in advance and came
items.explanation: -saydı … -ırdı — “if I had… I would have.” Didn't know, didn't come.

options: If you have to go — go
If you had had to go, you would have gone
items.explanation: -meliyse — “if you have to.” Gitmeliysen: if you have to go.

options: Eda will come and we'll buy a cake
If Eda had come, we would have bought a cake
If Eda's going to come, let's buy a cake
items.explanation: -ecekse — “if going to.” The plan is still ahead.

exercises.instruction: Sort them: is the door still open or already shut?

items.explanation: A tag on a tense (-mışsa, -yorsa, -ecekse, -meliyse) is a live “if.” -saydı … -ırdı is “if only,” the door is shut.

items.translation: If the tram's already coming — let's run!
items.explanation: The last vowel in geliyor is o, so -sa. No y needed: the form ends in a consonant.

items.translation: If Eda's going to come, let's buy a cake.
items.explanation: In gelecek the last vowel is e — tag -se. Gelseydi is “if only,” but the plan is still alive.

items.translation: If you have to go — go, I'm not keeping you.
items.explanation: Gitmeli ends in a vowel, so the tag attaches with a y: gitmeli-y-sen.

items.translation: If the landlord got the letter, he'll reply.
items.explanation: In almış the last vowel is ı — tag -sa. Alsaydı would shut the door: “if he had gotten it.”

items.translation: If I'd known in advance, I would have come.
items.explanation: After “if only” the second half is in past regret too: -ırdı, gelirdim.

items.translation: If I had known in advance, I would have come.
items.explanation: English “had known” is not -dı + sa. Bildiysem = “if I did know.” Unreal: bil-se-ydi-m.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence. One or two bricks are extra.

items.translation: If you've already bought the ticket, I'll come.
items.explanation: The door is open — a tag on the tense: almışsan gelirim.

items.translation: If I'd left earlier, I wouldn't have missed the tram.
items.explanation: If only — -saydım, and the second half in -ırdı: kaçırmazdım.

items.translation: If you're going to get up early tomorrow, go to bed now.
items.explanation: Plan ahead — -acaksan: kalkacaksan.

exercises.instruction: Five minutes to the concert: get five tags in place in time.

items.explanation: You don't know if he got it — a live “if” in the past: almışsa.
In geliyor the last vowel is o — tag -sa: geliyorsa.
Plan ahead — gelecekse, with -se because of the vowel e.
The concert's over, you regret it — if only: bilseydim.
Gitmeli ends in a vowel — you need y: gitmeliysen.

exercises.instruction: Mini check: five questions, 80% to pass.

items.prompt: You don't know if Eda has read the message. “If she's read it, she'll reply” is…
items.explanation: She may have read it already — a tag on the past: okumuşsa.
In kalacak the last vowel is a — tag -sa, person “we” — -k: kalacaksak.

items.statement: “Eğer tramvay geliyor, koşalım!” is correct: eğer already means “if.”
items.explanation: Eğer is optional. The real “if” is the tag: (Eğer) tramvay geliyorsa koşalım!

items.statement: “Alsaydın gelirdim” means: you might still buy a ticket, and I'll come.
items.explanation: -saydın … -irdim — “if only.” You didn't buy it — I'm not coming, the door is shut.

items.prompt: “If I'd known, I would have told you”: Bilseydim ___.
items.explanation: The second half of “if only” is in -(I)rdI: söylerdim.
